title: How Migraines Work
summary: Josh and Chuck open with a fan request from Aaron Cooper, who has migraines with aura and hemiplegic-style symptoms, and discuss what migraines are: a neurobiological condition involving neuropeptides, pain receptor sensitization, vasodilation, and blood vessel leakage. They cover triggers (food, smells, weather, sleep, hormones, stress, exercise), migraine types (classic, common, chronic, ocular, abdominal, cluster, thunderclap), diagnosis (MRI, CT, spinal tap), symptoms, treatments (acute drugs like Excedrin Migraine, Imitrex/sumatriptan, nasal sprays, injections; preventive off-label drugs such as blood pressure medications, antidepressants, and anticonvulsants; supplements like butterbur, CoQ10, feverfew; alternative therapies), famous people said to have had migraines, and the etymology of migraine (hemicrania, megrim). The episode ends with a listener mail about first kisses and a late-bloomer message.

segments.title: Fan request intro and Aaron Cooper's migraines
segments.summary: Hosts open with a fan request from Aaron Cooper, who has migraines with alternating sides, triggers, aura warnings, and a dark-room-and-nap treatment.

segments.title: What migraines are and how they differ from headaches
segments.summary: Migraines are not simply headaches caused by vasoconstriction; they were once thought to be vasodilation. Migraines are prevalent, can last from minutes to days, and are now classified as a neurobiological condition. Prevalence and family inheritance are discussed.

segments.title: Neuropeptides, pain receptors and the migraine cascade
segments.summary: Hosts describe the current understanding: a trigger activates pain receptors, neuropeptides act as neuromodulators that amplify pain signaling, blood vessels relax, and possible leakage and swelling follow, with aura thought to stem from vasodilation.

segments.title: Migraine triggers
segments.summary: Triggers vary by person and include foods (caffeine, alcohol, cheese, MSG), strong smells, behaviors like sleep changes, stress, sex, and exercise, weather and barometric pressure changes, loud noises and flashing lights, and hormones.

segments.title: Types of migraines and related headaches
segments.summary: Classic migraine with aura, common migraine without aura, chronic migraine (more than fifteen a month), ocular migraine, and abdominal migraine in children are described, along with cluster headaches and thunderclap headaches.

segments.title: Diagnosis and spinal tap
segments.summary: Diagnosis involves ruling out other conditions with MRI, CT scans, and spinal taps, since migraines cannot be fully explained. Hosts joke about spinal taps and the needle's size.

segments.title: Migraine treatments: acute, preventive, and alternative
segments.summary: Acute treatments include Excedrin Migraine (aspirin, acetaminophen, caffeine) taken early, and sumatriptan (Imitrex) nasal sprays and injections. Preventive off-label drugs include blood pressure medications, antidepressants, and calcium channel blockers. Supplements such as butterbur, CoQ10, and feverfew, plus massage, yoga, and acupuncture, are mentioned.

segments.title: Famous migraine sufferers and the word's etymology
segments.summary: A migraine personality theory is discussed, with famous people like Virginia Woolf, Nietzsche, Freud, Monet, Elvis, and Cervantes said to have had migraines, and Percy Harvin is mentioned. The word migraine comes from hemicrania and megrim.
